title: AP launches a tracker of Trump’s presidential promises
description_short: The Associated Press published a tracker of Donald Trump’s presidential promises on January 20, 2025.
description_medium: On January 20, 2025, the Associated Press published “Tracking Trump’s presidential promises,” a project that follows the status of Trump’s campaign promises. AP later described the tracker as following promises that were kept, stalled, or in progress. This supports a description of AP’s reporting project, not the older claims about ambiguous criteria, persistent exposure, or credibility costs. The supplied March 4, 2026 date is not corroborated by the source metadata.
description_long: On January 20, 2025, Associated Press journalists Eunice Esomonu, Humera Lodhi and Calvin Woodward published “Tracking Trump’s presidential promises,” an AP project about promises made by Donald Trump. AP describes the project as a tracker of what has been kept, stalled or remains in progress. This supports a record of AP’s reporting product; it does not itself establish that Trump broke a promise, changed the rules for judging one, or incurred credibility costs. The supplied workbench entries attach the same tracker URL and March 4, 2026 date to several characterizations, but identify no individual promise, benchmark, dated status row or archived update. The sources therefore do not substantiate the older claims that the tracking architecture sustained exposure, that Trump’s criteria were ambiguous, or that a delivery narrative lost durability. This proposal narrows the card to AP’s public tracker and uses the project’s publication date. Any later outcome should be described with a specific promise, AP’s dated status and the evidence AP cites. The tracker is an ongoing product and may change; this card records its launch, not a current count or promise status.

title: Manafort’s Ukraine political work preceded his Trump campaign role
description_short: A DOJ report documents Paul Manafort’s work for Ukraine’s Party of Regions and his later role on Trump’s 2016 campaign.
description_medium: Special Counsel Robert Mueller’s 2019 report says Paul Manafort did political work supporting Ukraine’s Party of Regions in 2005 and advised President Viktor Yanukovych from 2010 to 2014. The same report says Manafort joined Donald Trump’s campaign on March 29, 2016, and resigned on August 19, 2016. These records establish political consulting and campaign roles; they do not substantiate the original claim that Manafort helped Russia annex Crimea or control Ukraine.
description_long: The Special Counsel’s report describes Manafort’s pre-campaign Ukraine work in its account of Russian election interference. It says that in 2005 he did political work supporting the Party of Regions and later served as a close political adviser to Viktor Yanukovych, who was Ukraine’s president from 2010 until 2014. The report separately documents Manafort’s role on the Trump campaign: campaign leadership announced him as convention manager on March 29, 2016; he later became campaign chairman and chief strategist; he resigned on August 19 after reporting about his Ukraine consulting. These facts support a narrower account of Manafort’s prior political work and Trump campaign service. They do not establish that he assisted Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea, controlled Ukraine, or helped arrange a referendum there. Those more serious claims require evidence tied to specific acts and cannot be inferred from his work for a Ukrainian political party or from his later campaign position. The proposed date range identifies his documented Trump campaign service; the earlier Ukraine work is background context from 2005 to 2014, not an adjudication of Russian operations.

source_support.source_excerpt: “In 2005, Akhmetov had Manafort engage in political work supporting the Party of Regions.” The DOJ-hosted Mueller Report excerpt also states Manafort was a close political adviser to Yanukovych from 2010–2014 and served on the Trump campaign from March 29 to August 19, 2016.

source_support.limitation: The excerpt documents consulting and campaign roles; it does not say Manafort assisted the Crimean annexation or referendum.

title: Moving truck reported outside Kushner home on January 7, 2021
description_short: Two reports described a branded moving truck and boxes outside Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump’s Washington home.
description_medium: On January 7, 2021, Business Insider reported an orange College Hunks Hauling Junk truck outside Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump’s Washington home and boxes being carried from the garage. Vanity Fair also described the truck and boxes. The reporting supports the sighting, not the original claim that junk was removed, what service was booked, or why the activity occurred.
description_long: Business Insider reported on January 7, 2021, that an orange truck carrying the College Hunks Hauling Junk brand was outside Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump’s Washington residence. The story described a person carrying boxes from the garage and noted that the truck could reflect removal of unwanted items or preparations to move. Vanity Fair separately described an orange company truck and boxes at the home that Thursday. The reporting supports the limited claim that a branded truck was seen outside the residence while boxes were carried out. It does not establish what service the crew performed, whether items were discarded or donated, whether the couple had booked a move, or what prompted the activity. It also does not connect the sighting to Trump administration business, public funds, or the January 6 attack. This proposal therefore avoids the original claim that “junk” was removed and treats the event as a brief reported household sighting involving the president’s daughter and son-in-law. The contemporaneous reports are the evidence; later interpretations of the family’s plans are not established by the truck alone.

source_support.source_excerpt: “a bright-orange truck emblazoned with the well-known College Hunks Hauling Junk brand”; the article says this could reflect the couple getting rid of unwanted items or preparing to leave, without determining which.

No public funds, Trump administration business, or causal connection to January 6 was established.
